_comment: MorseTrainer release history, newest first. The website reads this file from GitHub (main branch) to render its changelog and the version badge. Add a new release at the TOP and keep 'version' equal to MT_VERSION in MT_Version.h.

changes: New ABC tab: a Morse reference with two pages - A-Z / 0-9 / punctuation as dit/dah bars, and every Q-code, prosign and abbreviation from CW Essentials with its meaning.
Tap any entry in the ABC tab to hear it at your keyer WPM (prosigns are sent run-together) - the LEDs flash along with it.

New Fist Check on the OPS tab: send anything and get a live read-out of your timing - speed, dit steadiness, dah:dit ratio, and element / letter / word spacing against the ideal 1 / 3 / 7, with a score and a tip. Straight key gets the full analysis; iambic checks your spacing.
Falling Letters now deals from a shuffled A-Z bag: every letter appears once before any letter repeats, and a letter already falling isn't dropped again.
All games now use the hardware random generator again - playing Phrases used to switch the whole device to a weaker one until reboot.
Support for Waveshare board V2: the new CST3530 touch controller is now auto-detected at boot alongside the V1 CST328.
One single firmware now runs on both board revisions - no separate builds.
New game Morse Memory: the device plays a growing letter sequence and you key it back; one wrong letter ends the run, with Beginner, Intermediate and Expert levels.
Morse Trace gains a CUSTOM mode where you choose which aids to show (letter, dit/dah bars, sound); at least one must stay on.
Callsign Rush adds a LETTER ONLY level: the callsign is shown with no audio or bars and you send it from memory against a 12 s clock.
17 new NeoPixel effects including Comet, Scanner, Fire, Twinkle, Aurora, Plasma, Lightning, Matrix, Lava and Meteor.
The OPS tab now shows CW Essentials and Morse Memory as full-size cards, and the Reset Scores button moved to the CFG tab.
Callsign Rush checks each letter as you send it, the timer only runs while you are sending, and Expert now keeps the callsign hidden until you miss.
Callsign Rush Beginner keeps the letters you already got right after a mistake, and the game over screen shows the callsign you missed.
Falling Letters Beginner falls more slowly and spawns letters less often, and the first letter now appears right away.
QSO Simulator ignores spaces when checking your reply, so you no longer need exact word-gap timing.
Scores in Callsign Rush and Falling Letters are now saved when you leave a game with EXIT.
New Straight Key Timing option on the KEY tab: AUTO (adaptive, learns your speed) or WPM-BASED (uses the WPM setting).
Paddles and straight key are muted while a game plays Morse, so your sidetone no longer plays over the playback and stray keying is ignored.
The decoder now drops a character as soon as your keying can no longer match any valid Morse code, so one stray element doesn't spoil the next letter.
After a wrong answer in CW Essentials and Callsign Rush, keying already in progress is discarded so the retry starts clean.
Larger touch areas for the CLR, EXIT, LIST, BACK and page buttons.
Fixed Morse playback in Callsign Rush, CW Essentials, QSO Simulator and Morse Trace: gaps between characters were too long, so playback was slower than the set WPM.
CW Essentials now has 65 abbreviations and Q-codes, ordered by how often they are used in real CW QSOs.
Guided and Practice modes open a paged phrase list: pick one phrase to repeat or choose Shuffle All.
Shuffle goes through every phrase once before any repeats, instead of cycling through the same few.
New LIST button in phrase modes takes you back to the phrase picker.
Swiping no longer changes tabs, so dragging a slider on CFG can't jump you to another tab.
CW Essentials redesigned: My Callsign teaches each letter on its own, then builds up longer and longer runs until you send the whole callsign.
Two correct rounds in a row move you to the next callsign stage.
Targets show done, current and remaining letters in different colours, with reference bars for the current letter and live bars as you key.
Game cards on the OPS tab are more compact and no longer have icons.
Fixed CW Essentials so that leaving the game returns to the main screen and the home screen decodes your keying again.
New game CW Essentials, with three modes: My Callsign, Phrases Guided (hear it, then key it) and Phrases Practice.
Phrases include common prosigns, Q-codes and abbreviations such as CQ, QTH, 73 and RST, each shown with its meaning.
CW Essentials keeps a best score, shown on its OPS tab card and cleared by Reset Scores.
Swapped the WPM buttons on the KEY tab so minus is on the left and plus is on the right.
New LEDs setting on the CFG tab to set how many NeoPixels are connected, from 1 to 60 (default 20).
Settings no longer back up to or restore from the SD card automatically at boot; backup and restore are now manual only.
SD settings backups now include LED count, screen flip and keyer timing, and restoring applies them right away.
WiFi credentials are now stored on the SD card.
Reset Scores now also clears your LEARN mode progress.
New NeoPixel modes: Steady, Breathe, Starfield, Chase and Rainbow, plus separate brightness sliders for key flash and background effects.
LED mode Off now turns the LEDs fully off, including key and game flashes.
Maximum WPM raised from 40 to 60.
Hidden keyer timing menu (tap the WPM card 12 times) to adjust character gap, word gap and dit/dah threshold.
EXIT buttons added to Callsign Rush and Falling Letters, and a Reset Scores button with confirmation added to the OPS tab.
New FLIP switch on the CFG tab rotates the screen and touch input 180 degrees.
Hold both paddles at power-on to turn screen flip back off.
Hidden easter egg: tap the CALL card 7 times.
First release for the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-2.8, with a dark touch UI and HOME, KEY, OPS, CFG and NET tabs.
Iambic A/B keyer with adjustable WPM, plus a straight-key mode that adapts to your speed, with live decoding on the home screen.
I2S sidetone with adjustable pitch and volume, and 20 NeoPixels with key flash, WPM meter and ambient modes.
Four practice games with difficulty levels and saved high scores: Falling Letters, Callsign Rush, Morse Trace (with a guided LEARN mode) and QSO Simulator.
Firmware updates from the SD card, and settings backup and restore.
